decisions.mark: states that staleness is THREE distinguishable axes rather than one flag, and names them
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "A clew index knows it is out of date along three separate axes." followed by "**Data axis (sources changed).**", "**Schema axis (version mismatch).**", "**Code axis (the running process predates its source).**" | WHY: The answer states staleness is three separate axes (data, schema, code) rather than one flag, names each, and notes the remedy depends on which axis is stale. || QUOTE: "A clew index knows it is out of date along three separate axes." followed by "**Data axis (sources changed).**", "**Schema axis (version mismatch).**", "**Code axis (the running process predates its source).**" | WHY: The answer explicitly states staleness is three separate axes and names data, schema, and code, noting the remedy differs per axis. || QUOTE: A clew index knows it is out of date along three separate axes. ... **Data axis (sources changed).** ... **Schema axis (version mismatch).** ... **Code axis (the running process predates its source).** | WHY: The answer explicitly says staleness has three separate axes and names them as data, schema and code.

decisions.mark: explains that each axis is cleared by a DIFFERENT action — a rebuild for data, a client restart for code — which is why one flag would not have been enough
decisions.detail: QUOTE: The code message says a rebuild cannot fix it and the MCP client must be restarted. | WHY: The answer gives per-axis remedies (refresh for data, restart for code), but never says that distinct remedies are why a single flag would not have been enough. || QUOTE: The code message says a rebuild cannot fix it and the MCP client must be restarted. | WHY: The answer gives per-axis remedies (refresh for data, restart for code), but it never says that this difference is why a single flag would not have been enough. || QUOTE: The code message says a rebuild cannot fix it and the MCP client must be restarted. | WHY: The answer gives per-axis remedies (refresh for data, restart for code), but it never states that the different remedies are the reason one flag would not have been enough.

decisions.mark: identifies that the schema axis can be UNRESOLVABLE — when the index is newer than the server, no rebuild clears it, because rebuilding re-stamps the same newer version
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "The direction matters. decisions.mark: states the read/write asymmetry on the code axis: READS stay current because query tools open the database per call, while a BUILD through a stale process writes old pipeline logic
decisions.detail: QUOTE: A write from a process that predates its source is refused with "Nothing was written," and `force` does not override the refusal. A write from a process that predates its source is refused with "Nothing was written," and `force` does not override the refusal.
